title: Burke gets Capitol to raise his royalty from four to five percent; end of tape
summary: After the Astaire show, Burke argued for a higher graduated royalty and won 5 percent; Jones, who never knew royalties escalate, was happy with a penny, and Dance ends the session to drive to Connecticut.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But a lot of things like that he did then. Another thing about Capitol, when we got out there and we started doing the Fred Astaire show, well the royalties was graduated up, you know, like --

Yeah, so that's what I was thinking, you know, so this guy said -- so Wally said, 'Well, we're happy to have you with the family and I hope you're happy.' So Sammy said, 'Oh, we're happy, but we could be happier.' So Wally said, 'Well, what do you mean by that, you could be happier?' He said, 'Well, if that 4 percent was moved up to 5 percent.' He said, 'Yeah, but you've got a contract.' So he says, 'Oh, but you said that if I could be happier, you know. You said you hope I'm happy. I said yeah, but I could be happier.' He said, 'I'll tell you what you do. Come by here tomorrow at 2:00 o'clock and we'll talk.' And he gave him the 5 percent.
You know, well that is really --

Here's a guy that's fighting for you. Now, he don't have to tell me all of these things, you know, but he's fighting for me, you know what I mean? All the way. Sammy says, 'Get it now, while them records are hot. Who knows what's going to be next year.'
He says, 'You may be dead next year.'
That's right, you know. Yeah, always try.
Also he's saying things that you wouldn't want to say, probably, you know.
Oh, yeah, and I couldn't say, and I wouldn't know how to say.
Well, I mean Earl's the same. Earl doesn't want to do that kind of thing either.
I didn't know that the thing graduates. I didn't know nothing about that, you know.
If they had given me a penny I'd have been happy. It's more than I ever got.
Yeah. Jonah, I'm going to cut it off, because we've got to drive to Connecticut.
